title: Remove fish scales without cutting the skin
instruction: Remove the attached scales from the exposed side of the fish with the scaler, without cutting its skin. Leave the fish on the board and release it.
context: Descaling needs firm support and tail-to-head scraping against overlapping scales, with enough pressure to lift scales without damaging the skin.
setup: A 260 mm, approximately 250 g prepared whole fish lies on a fixed 250 x 300 x 8 mm wooden board. Its underside is already descaled; 26 equal-area scaled sectors remain on the exposed side. A loose 87 g stainless scaler with a 24 x 28 mm serrated head and a handle offset 30 mm above the head lies clear of the board. Two rigid 40 x 6 x 1 mm stainless-steel precision finger extensions per arm have a 4 N jaw limit. The starting layout is fixed; no fish or tool is attached to the board.
scoring: After 3 seconds with open fingers at least 65 mm clear, score the fraction of 26 initially scaled sectors with all scales detached from the skin. Loose flakes may remain; rinsing is outside the task. Zero for torn or crushed skin, a fish no longer supported upright on its prepared side on the board, or incomplete release. Inspect photographs and use a blunt probe to distinguish loose flakes from attached scales.
fidelity: A rigid fish, including its tail, carries skin patches with normal, shear and bending compliance and 26 retained scale groups. Loaded tail-to-head tooth contact releases groups; excess skin compression or broken skin joints loses credit. This approximates scraping and damage, not flesh deformation, tail tearing or microscopic scale mechanics. Contact-checked, force-limited pinch joints approximate finger friction.
reset_notes: Use a fresh prepared fish with its underside descaled and its exposed side scaled. Remove loose scales from the board and scaler before resetting. Fixed layout; no object jitter.
